headers.//: Snapshots are the ONLY genuinely immutable data here. Their path carries the bake date (data/snapshots/2026-09-05/...), so a re-bake writes a NEW path and can never need to invalidate an old one. A year is safe.

Everything else under data/ lives at a STABLE path -- data/roads.geojson, data/trees.geojson, data/highways.geojson are overwritten in place by their bake scripts. Marking these immutable was the first version of this file and it is a trap: a re-bake would deploy correctly and never reach anyone who had already visited, for a year, with no way to tell them apart from a cache miss. One hour, revalidated, so a rebuild lands on the next visit while repeat loads in one session still come from cache.
Third-party libraries, pinned by version in the path.
Application code. Ten minutes, matching what GitHub Pages sends, so behaviour here and on Pages stays comparable.
